info.title: Simulator.Company API
info.description:
The Simulator.Company API lets an integration read and change a workspace: its **actors** (every
object is an actor — a record built from an **account template**), the **edges** that link actors into a
graph, the **accounts** and **transactions** that carry balances, and the **reactions**,
**attachments** and **access rules** around them.

This is the **public integration contract** (beta). Every method here is a support promise:
incompatible changes come with a documented migration and a compatibility window.

## Names in the API

The API keeps older names for two entities the product renames: an **account template** is a
*form* in method and field names (`form/*`, `formId`, `forms`), and a **Smart Form** is an
*application* (`application/*`, `app_*`). This reference uses the product names in prose and the
API names in code.

## Making a request

The API is [JSON-RPC 2.0](https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification) over HTTPS. There is one endpoint —
every method is a `POST` to it, and the method name travels in the body:

```http
POST /api/2.0/rpc
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: ApiKey <key>

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": "1",
  "method": "actor/get",
  "params": { "accId": "f54fd368-6ebf-427a-89a3-72283e320f6a", "actorId": "a55cd656-e33e-425c-9971-b0a258bfd914" }
}
```

- `id` **must be a string**. It is echoed in the response so you can match answers to calls.
- `params` is always an object of named parameters.
- The reference shows each method at its own anchor (`/rpc#actor/get`); the fragment is only an
  anchor — every call goes to `/api/2.0/rpc`.

A response carries either `result` or `error`, never both:

```json
{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": "1", "result": { "id": "a55cd656-e33e-425c-9971-b0a258bfd914", "title": "Order #1042" } }
```

## Authentication

Send credentials in the `Authorization` header.

| Scheme | Header | Acts as |
|--------|--------|---------|
| API key | `Authorization: ApiKey <key>` | The API user the key was issued for, in **one** workspace |
| User token | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` | A person, through their SuperAdmin (account.corezoid.com) OAuth session |

An **API key** is bound to the workspace it was issued in, so every call made with it must name
that workspace in `accId`; a method that takes no `accId` cannot be called with a key. A key also
carries **scopes**, and each method lists the scope it needs (see below). A **user token** is not
scope-checked: the call runs with that person's own access.

Either way, authentication only gets you to the method. What you can see and change is decided per
object by its **access rules** (`view`, `modify`, `remove`, `sign`, `execute`); a call on an object
the caller has no access to fails with `accessDenied`.

## Scopes

| Scope | Grants |
|-------|--------|
| `actors.readonly` / `actors.management` | Read / change actors, edges, graphs and layers, accounts, counters, transactions, reactions, access rules and Smart Forms |
| `forms.readonly` / `forms.management` | Read / change account templates |
| `transfers.readonly` / `transfers.management` | Read / create transfers between accounts |
| `attachments.readonly` / `attachments.management` | Read / change file attachments |
| `workspaces.readonly` | Read the workspace, its users and groups |

## Identifiers

| Value | Format | Example |
|-------|--------|---------|
| `accId` — workspace | UUID string | `f54fd368-6ebf-427a-89a3-72283e320f6a` |
| `actorId`, `edgeId`, account `nameId` | UUID string | `a55cd656-e33e-425c-9971-b0a258bfd914` |
| `formId`, `currencyId`, `userId` | integer | `19` |
| `ref` | your own string key, unique within an account template | `order-1042` |

Most entities can be addressed by your own `ref` instead of their id — see the `…/by-ref/…` methods.
Refs make imports safe to retry: a second create with the same `ref` in the same account template is refused
instead of creating a duplicate.

## Shaping responses

List and get methods accept two response-only parameters:

- **`fields`** — a projection: keep only these keys (`data.<key>` narrows a template field). It never
  adds anything.
- **`with`** — opt into related entities that are not on the record itself, e.g. `owner`,
  `attachments`, `attachments:user`. It never changes the type of a field that is already there.

Lists page with `limit` and `offset`. A list never reports a total; ask the sibling `…/count`
method with the same filter.

## Errors

On failure `result` is absent and `error` is set. **The HTTP status is still 200** — check the body.

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": "1",
  "error": {
    "code": 1,
    "message": "access denied: no view access to the actor",
    "data": { "reason": "accessDenied", "reqId": "d3b07384d113edec49eaa6238ad5ff00" }
  }
}
```

Branch on `error.data.reason`, never on `message` — reasons are stable, messages are not.

| Reason | Code | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| `invalidParams` | -32602 | A parameter is missing or malformed; `message` names it |
| `notAuthorized` | 1 | Missing, expired or wrong credentials, or a key used outside its workspace |
| `accessDenied` | 1 | Authenticated, but the access rules do not allow this |
| `notAllowed` | 1 | The operation is not allowed here: the method is not available to this kind of caller, or the object refuses it (a read-only production environment, a system folder that cannot be renamed or deleted) |
| `notFound` | 1 | The object does not exist (or you cannot see it) |
| `alreadyExists` | 1 | A create collided with an object that already exists |
| `actorLocked` | 1 | Another write holds the actor; retry shortly |
| `timeout` | -32000 | The call ran out of time; it may or may not have been applied |
| `methodNotFound` | -32601 | No such method, or it is not part of the public API |

Quote `data.reqId` when you report a problem.

## Batches

[`batch`](#tag/batch) runs several calls in one request, in order — each item sees what the earlier
ones wrote, and an item can use an earlier result (`"useRefs": true`, then `"$0.id"`). With
`"isAtomic": true` the whole batch commits or rolls back together; only methods marked safe for
atomic batches are accepted there.

## Drawing a graph

A graph is drawn with ordinary actors and edges: the graph and each of its layers are actors of the
`Graphs` and `Layers` system account templates, and a layer is the canvas that places actors and edges at
positions.

1. **Look up the workspace's ids once.** `form/system/list` returns the `Graphs` and `Layers`
   templates (their ids differ per workspace); `edge_type/get` with `name: "hierarchy"` returns the
   edge type that links a graph to its layers and the editor uses for drawn links.
2. **Create the canvas** in one atomic batch: an `actor/create` of the `Graphs` template, an
   `actor/create` of the `Layers` template, and an `edge/create` of the hierarchy type from the graph to
   the layer. The layer actor's id is the `actorId` of every `graph/layer/…` method.
3. **Create and place the content** in one atomic batch: the actors (`actor/create`), the edges
   between them (`edge/create`), then `graph/layer/actors/manage` placing the actors at positions
   (graph units, y downward, snapped to 50), then a second `graph/layer/actors/manage` placing the
   edges between the placements the first one returned (`"$<i>.nodes.<n>.laId"`).
4. **Style it** with `graph/layer/actor_settings/save` and `graph/layer/edge_settings/save`, and set
   a background with `graph/layer/picture/update`.

Read it back with `graph/layer/actors/list` and `graph/layer/edges/list` (or
`graph/layer/skeleton/get` for a large layer), and walk the stored relations with `graph/get`.
`graph/layer/actors/manage` shows the full batch. To show a layer live to the people who have it
open, start a presentation with `graph/layer/presentation/start`.

## Building a Smart Form

A Smart Form (an *application* in the API) is an actor of the `Scripts` system template with a **develop** and a
**production** environment, each a folder tree of page configs, locale, view model, styles and
scripts. You edit develop; a release copies it into production, which is what users open.

1. **Create it** with `application/create` (`cduVersion: 2`, a `ref`): both environments come
   seeded with a start page. `application/install` creates one from a template instead.
2. **Write the pages** in develop with `app_folder/create` and `app_file/create` /
   `app_file/update` — page configs are checked against the CDU component catalog when saved.
   `application/struct` shows the tree and the ids. One page should declare the root route (`/`)
   for the short URL to open something.
3. **Connect the backend** (optional) with `application/env/update` for each environment, or let
   `corezoid/project/create` give the Smart Form a Corezoid project of its own.
4. **Preview** develop with `page/render` (`envTitle: "develop"`).
5. **Publish** with `release/create` from develop to production. The release checks every page and
   route; the first one also gives the Smart Form its short URL key (`route/key/set` picks it yourself).
6. **Open it**: `route/key/get` returns the key, `<app>/sf/<appKey>` is the address, and
   `page/render` / `page/submit` serve and submit its pages. `release/rollback` returns production
   to an earlier release.

methods.name: actor/get
methods.summary: Retrieves details of a specific actor by ID
methods.description:
Returns one actor by its id: its title, the account template it was built from, and its
template field values (`data`).

The caller needs `view` access to the actor. By default the response carries the actor's own
columns only; related information is opt-in through `with` (unknown values are ignored):

| `with` value | Adds |
|--------------|------|
| `owner` | `owner` and `ownerId` — the actor's owner |
| `user` | `user` — the user who created the actor |
| `privs` | `privs` — what the **caller** may do with this actor |
| `access`, `defaultAccess` | the actor's access rules / its account template's default rules |
| `attachments`, `attachments:user` | attached files (and who attached them) |
| `lastReaction`, `lastComment` (`:user`) | the most recent reaction / comment |
| `reactionsStats`, `unreadReactions`, `unread`, `starred` | reaction counters and the caller's read state |
| `executionState` | the approval workflow stage, for actors with sign/execute rules |
| `notificationSettings` | the caller's notification settings for this actor |
| `meeting` | the live call on the actor: room, participants, last transcript line |
| `forms` | every account template attached to the actor, in order (templates the caller cannot view come back as `accessDenied` stubs) |
| `avatar` | what an avatar needs beyond `picture`: `systemObjType`/`systemObjId` (what a system actor is the twin of: a user or the workspace), for a user actor that user's SuperAdmin id `systemObjSAId`, and the account template's `formPicture`/`formType` (the fallback). A source that does not apply or no longer exists is omitted |

Use `fields` to cut the answer down, e.g. `["id", "title", "data.amount"]` returns only those
keys and only the `amount` field of `data`.

To look an actor up by your own key instead of its id, use `actor/by-ref/get`.

schema.description: Projection: keep only these keys; data.<key> keeps one template field

Related data to add: owner, user, privs, access[:compact], defaultAccess, attachments[:user], lastReaction[:user], lastComment[:user], reactionsStats, unreadReactions, unread, starred, executionState, notificationSettings, meeting, forms, avatar

methods.name: form/get
methods.summary: Retrieves details of a specific account template
methods.description:
Returns one account template (account templates are called *forms* in the API): its settings
and, in `form`, the full template body — the `sections` with every template field an actor of
this template carries. A field's `id` is the key of its value in actor `data`.

The caller needs `view` access to the account template. Optional includes via `with`:

| `with` value | Adds |
|--------------|------|
| `editor` | `canModify`, `editToken` (pass it to `form/update` as `expectedEditToken`) and `accountTemplateEditor` |
| `parents` | `parents` — the ancestor chain, immediate parent first; ancestors the caller cannot view are `accessDenied` stubs, and a complete chain ends with a template without `parentId` |

To look an account template up by your own key, use `form/by-ref/get`.

schema.description: Optional includes. Supported: 'editor' (write capability/token), 'parents' (full ancestor chain)

accessDenied.description: Whether the current user has no view access to this ancestor template

losslessUpdate.description: Whether account template updates preserve unrecognized JSON fields and scalar encodings

optionResolver.description: Whether typed dynamic option resolution is available

supportedOptionSources.description: Option source types the resolver executes; all others fail closed as unsupported

accountTemplateEditor.description: Template editor capabilities of this server (with editor)

canModify.description: Whether the current user may modify this non-system account template

canRemove.description: Whether the current user may delete this non-system account template (form/list only)

collapsed.description: Whether the account template is shown collapsed in the template editor

editToken.description: Opaque optimistic-concurrency token for the full account template write footprint

form.description: The template body: sections with their fields, settings and other editor keys (not returned by form/list)

isDefault.description: Whether this is a workspace default account template

isTemplate.description: Whether the account template is live; false once it is deleted

ownerId.description: User who owns the account template

ownerName.description: Owner's nick (form/list only); absent when the owner's user row is gone or could not be read

parentId.description: Parent account template in the template tree

parents.description: Full ancestor chain, immediate-parent-first (only when with contains 'parents'); empty array for a root template

position.description: Position of the account template in the template editor

ref.description: Your own key for the account template, unique within the workspace

status.description: Approval status: verified, rejected or pending

type.description: Kind of a platform-owned account template (system or connector); absent for custom templates

examples.name: With the edit token and the parent chain

methods.name: graph/layer/actors/list
methods.summary: Lists actor placements of a layer with pagination
methods.description:
Lists the actors placed on a layer, most recently placed first, one page at a time. Each row is a
**placement**: its `laId`, where it sits (`position` in graph units and the same point as a
`cellPosition`), how it is drawn (`layerSettings`, `polygon`, `areaPicture`) and, in `actor`, the
actor itself with the shape of `actor/get`.

The caller needs `view` access to the layer actor (`actorId`). A placement whose actor the caller
cannot view is still listed, as a stub of `laId`, `id`, `position` and `accessDenied: true`, so the
layer's layout stays whole. One actor can be placed on a layer more than once; each placement is
its own row. `limit` is at most 1000 (default 50); page with `offset`. `fields` and `with`
shape `actor` as in `actor/get` — `with: ["formTitle"]` adds the account template's title.

`hole: true` marks a placeholder for an actor that is not known yet; `closedHole` marks a placement
that closed one (see the [graph tag](#tag/graph)). The edges between placements are listed by
`graph/layer/edges/list`; the counts are in `graph/layer/stats/get`. To fetch only some
placements by `laId`, use `graph/layer/elements/list`; to read a large layer's layout fast, use
`graph/layer/skeleton/get`.

schema.description: Maximum number of items to return
Projection of each placement's actor, as in actor/get
Related entities to include in node responses (formTitle adds each node's account template title, avatar its avatar sources)

accessDenied.description: Whether the caller has no view access to the actor; the placement then carries only laId, id and position

isRoot.description: Whether this is the actor's primary account template (its formId)

parentId.description: Parent account template in the template tree

sorting.description: Position of the account template on the actor (ascending)

forms.description: Ordered account templates attached to the actor (opt-in via with:["forms"])

hole.description: Whether the actor is a graph hole placeholder

type.description: Subject type: user, group, api, anonymous or system

lastComment.description: Most recent visible comment, including replies (opt-in via with:["lastComment"] or with:["lastComment:user"])

type.description: Subject type: user, group, api, anonymous or system

lastReaction.description: Most recent reaction (opt-in via with:["lastReaction"] or with:["lastReaction:user"])

eventType.description: System event the line records (join, leave, handRaise, recording, …); absent on spoken lines

id.description: Stable line identifier (UUID); absent on lines written by the legacy server

isSystemMessage.description: Whether the line is a system event rather than speech

parentSaId.description: SuperAdmin id of the quoted line's speaker

parentUserId.description: Platform user id of the quoted line's speaker

parentUserMetaInfo.description: Profile metadata of the quoted line's speaker

parentUserNick.description: Display name of the quoted line's speaker

reactionId.description: Reaction (comment) the line was posted as, if any

text.description: Spoken or system text of the line

timestamp.description: When the line was spoken (Unix seconds)

userId.description: Platform user id of the speaker

lastTranscription.description: Newest line of the live transcript, or null

type.description: Subject type: user, group, api, anonymous or system

participants.description: Platform users connected to the room (one entry per device)

activeRecording.description: Whether the room is being recorded

creationTime.description: When the room was created (Unix seconds)

fileName.description: File the recording is written to

startedById.description: Platform user id of who started the recording

title.description: Title the recording will be filed under

recording.description: The recording in progress, if any

apiCount.description: Groups only: number of API users in the group

isMember.description: Groups only: whether the caller is a member

isOwner.description: Groups only: whether the caller owns the group

isTest.description: Whether this is a test account

logins.description: Logins: login, type and create_time of each (e-mail, phone, OAuth provider); password hashes, API key tokens and webhook URLs are never returned

type.description: Subject type: user, group, api, anonymous or system

userCount.description: Groups only: number of users in the group

recordingStartBy.description: User who started the current recording

metadata.description: Room metadata: recording and transcription state

room.description: The live LiveKit room, or null when no call is running

meeting.description: The actor's live meeting: room, participants, last transcript line (opt-in via with:["meeting"])

snooze.description: Snooze period in minutes (null if not snoozed)

notificationSettings.description: The caller's notification settings for this actor (opt-in via with:["notificationSettings"])

type.description: Subject type: user, group, api, anonymous or system

ownerId.description: Owner identifier (opt-in via with:["owner"] or fields:["ownerId"])

ds.description: Is asked to sign the object with a digital signature

execute.description: Is asked to carry out (execute) the object

modify.description: Can change the object and its access rules

sign.description: Is asked to approve (sign) the object

privs.description: What the caller may do with this actor (opt-in via with:["privs"])

reactionsStats.description: Reaction counters by reaction type (opt-in via with:["reactionsStats"])

readonly.description: Whether the actor is read-only: attachments cannot be added to or removed from it

ref.description: Your own key for the actor, unique within its account template

starred.description: Whether the caller starred the actor (opt-in via with:["starred"])

startDate.description: Start of the actor's period (Unix seconds); defaults to the creation time

status.description: Approval status, e.g. verified, pending or rejected

systemObjId.description: Linked system object id (opt-in via with:["avatar"])

systemObjSAId.description: SuperAdmin id of the linked user, for its SA avatar URL (opt-in via with:["avatar"])

systemObjType.description: Linked system object type ('user' for a user actor) (opt-in via with:["avatar"])

unread.description: Whether the calling user has never viewed this actor

unreadReactions.description: Number of reactions the caller has not read (opt-in via with:["unreadReactions"])

type.description: Subject type: user, group, api, anonymous or system

user.description: User who created the actor (opt-in via with:["user"])

actor.description: Actor details (absent when access is denied)

areaPicture.description: Area picture stretched over the placement

x.description: Column: A–Z for the first 26 columns right of the origin, then A1–Z1, A2…; a leading minus left of it (-A is the first)

y.description: Row: 1, 2, … from the origin down; -1, -2, … above it

cellPosition.description: The same position as a grid cell

matched.description: Hole conditions the closing actor satisfies

total.description: Non-empty data fields on the hole, each one a condition

closingProgress.description: How many of the hole's conditions the closing actor meets; null when the hole has none

holeActorId.description: Identifier of the hole actor closed by this placement

closedHole.description: The hole this placement closed, when it was dropped onto one

createdAt.description: When the actor was placed (Unix seconds)

hole.description: Whether the placed actor is a hole: a placeholder for an actor not known yet

laId.description: Placement identifier (laId); one actor can be placed on a layer more than once

anisotropy.description: Whether anisotropic texture filtering is enabled

expand.description: Whether the node is open in place, showing the content named by expandType

expandType.description: What an expanded node shows: cardView, chart, layer, profile, script (a Smart Form), actor (an actor page) or text
x-validation-rules: oneof=cardView chart layer profile script actor text

flaskView.description: Whether the node is rendered as a flask

fullScreen.description: Whether the expanded node is in full screen

height.description: Box height in graph units; same meaning as width

h.description: Height as a fraction of the source height

w.description: Width as a fraction of the source width

x.description: Left edge as a fraction of the source width

y.description: Top edge as a fraction of the source height

crop.description: Visible window into the source image

fit.description: How the bitmap fills its box (contain, cover, fill)

naturalHeight.description: Intrinsic height of the source image in pixels

naturalWidth.description: Intrinsic width of the source image in pixels

isCardView.description: Whether the node is rendered as a card

isTextNode.description: Whether the node is a text node

offset.description: How far an expanded node reaches past its cell. Typed here as {x, y}, while legacy clients and the graph editor store {top, right, bottom, left}: such a value reads back as {x: 0, y: 0}, and one sent here is stored as {x: 0, y: 0}. Do not send it

pin.description: Whether the node is pinned to this layer (cannot be dragged)

profile.description: Whether the profile view is shown

rotation.description: Clockwise rotation of an image placement, degrees

sizeGrade.description: Node size grade: S1 (one cell, the default), S2 or S3

userId.description: Author shown on a comment node: user id

userNick.description: Author shown on a comment node: display name

width.description: Box width in graph units: of a resizable placement (text, image), or of an actor's expanded content

zIndex.description: Stacking order: a higher value is drawn on top

position.description: Position on the layer in graph units

starred.description: Whether the caller starred this placement

list.description: Actor placements, most recently placed first

examples.name: The newest placements
examples.description: The newest placement is an actor the caller cannot see.
